issues.item: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: For a man-made disaster trauma in a 58-year-old forensic analyst, this item is only coherent if there was a significant physical injury. The rest of the selected profile does not support an injury-based presentation: the threat items emphasize environmental danger and vigilance (limited safe places, loud sounds, unfamiliar places), while the other appraisals are about coping failure and loss of capability rather than concrete bodily injury. With no memory or strategy items to anchor a physical-injury narrative, this appraisal stands out as clinically hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Threat: Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
issues.explanation: The profile is not coherent with the supplied cognitive formulation because all cross-node edges are inactive, which implies these components should not appear as tightly linked aspects of one maintaining pattern. However, the Threat items and Negative Appraisal items are strongly conceptually connected: perceiving the world as dangerous maps directly onto restricted safety zones and avoidance of unfamiliar places, creating an active Threat–Negative Appraisal linkage that contradicts the formulation.

issues.item: Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: Within the selected nodes, the content clusters into a classic mutually reinforcing danger/coping pattern rather than isolated components. 'World is a dangerous place' coheres directly with hypervigilance to sounds and avoidance of unfamiliar places, while 'Bad Coper' and 'No longer capable' reflect generalized post-trauma self-evaluation likely tied to the same threat response. With no active edges anywhere in the formulation, this degree of integration is inconsistent.

issues.item: Threat in Sounds: I am on high alert when I hear unexpected or loud sounds
issues.explanation: The formulation specifies no active edges, so the selected nodes should function as relatively isolated components rather than implying a tight linked syndrome. Here the Threat items and Negative Appraisal items form a classic connected PTSD pattern: danger-focused hypervigilance/startle and avoidance are closely mirrored by broad beliefs that the world is dangerous and that the self is incapable. This actively implies strong Threat↔Negative Appraisal linkage, which contradicts the fully disconnected formulation.

issues.item: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: Within Threat, the items are coherent with each other, and within Negative Appraisals the items are also coherent. The problem is cross-node/formulation consistency: the profile presents mutually reinforcing danger sensitivity and negative self/world beliefs despite all edges being inactive.

vignette: Carlos, a 58-year-old Latin American forensic analyst, has been struggling with the aftermath of a man-made disaster that occurred nearly six months ago. The event was sudden and violent-a massive explosion at his workplace-that left Carlos with lingering trauma. The night of the disaster is still vivid in Carlos's mind. He recalls the sound of shattering glass and the deafening boom that seemed to tear through the air, followed by an eerie silence. As he scrambled to safety amidst the chaos, he saw colleagues injured and bleeding, their faces contorted with pain and fear. This event has left him acutely aware of danger in unfamiliar environments. In the weeks following the disaster, Carlos found himself avoiding new or unfamiliar places because he could not assess the level of danger they posed. The uncertainty was paralyzing, and each step outside his comfort zone felt like a potential trap waiting to spring. He had come to believe that if he were to encounter another situation like the one at work, he would be unable to react appropriately, making him feel jumpy and easily startled. His body remains in constant tension, as though it is always on alert for the next threat. Even simple tasks now seem daunting. The slightest noise-a door slamming or a car backfiring-can send his heart racing and his palms sweating. He finds himself hypervigilant, constantly scanning his surroundings for signs of impending danger. This heightened state of alertness has also led to feelings of incompetence and self-doubt. Carlos was once known for his sharp analytical skills and his ability to remain calm under pressure. Now, he feels that his reactions since the event show that he is a lousy coper. He fears that this incident has revealed his true inadequacies and that he can no longer perform at the level he once did. This belief has begun to erode his confidence in himself as a forensic analyst. In addition, Carlos's worldview has shifted dramatically. The explosion made him realize how fragile life can be and how easily it can be shattered by human recklessness. He now sees the world as inherently dangerous, a place where threats lurk around every corner. This perception of danger is compounded by his belief that he cannot adequately protect himself or those close to him. The impact on his work has been significant. Carlos's avoidance of unfamiliar places means that he often declines field assignments and prefers to stay in familiar environments. His wife, who had always admired his resilience and strength, notices the change in him but doesn't quite understand why he is so different now. Their conversations have become strained as she struggles to bridge the gap between their present realities. What finally brought Carlos to seek help was a recent incident where he nearly missed an important meeting because he hesitated to leave his house for fear of encountering another threat. This realization that his condition was affecting not just his work but also his personal life pushed him to acknowledge that he needed support. Carlos is most afraid that the disaster will define him and rob him of who he once was-a competent, confident professional and a loving husband. He hopes for a return to some semblance of normalcy where he can feel safe again without having to constantly question his ability to cope with life's uncertainties.
